verses.zh: 末后的日子，耶和华殿的山必坚立，超乎诸山，高举过于万岭；万民都要流归这山。
verses.en: And in future days[NOTE:1] the Lord’s Temple Mount will be the most important mountain of all;[NOTE:2] it will be more prominent than other hills.[NOTE:3] People will stream to it.
notes: Cf. Isa 2:2. See the note at Gen 49:1.
Heb “will be established as the head of the mountains.”
Heb “it will be lifted up above the hills.”

verses.zh: 必有许多国的民前往，说：来吧，我们登耶和华的山，奔雅各　神的殿。主必将他的道教训我们；我们也要行他的路。因为训诲必出于锡安；耶和华的言语必出于耶路撒冷。
verses.en: Many nations will come, saying,“Come on! Let’s go up to the Lord’s mountain,to the temple of Jacob’s God,so he can teach us his waysand we can live by his laws.”[NOTE:1] For instruction will proceed from Zion,the Lord’s message from Jerusalem.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and we can walk in his paths.”
For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

verses.zh: 他必在多国的民中施行审判，为远方强盛的国断定是非。他们要将刀打成犁头，把枪打成镰刀。这国不举刀攻击那国；他们也不再学习战事。
verses.en: He will arbitrate[NOTE:1] between many peoplesand settle disputes between many[NOTE:2] distant nations.[NOTE:3] They will beat their swords into plowshares[NOTE:4] and their spears into pruning hooks.[NOTE:5] Nations will not use weapons[NOTE:6] against other nations,and they will no longer train for war.
notes: Or “judge.”
Or “mighty” (NASB); KJV, NAB, NIV, NRSV “strong”; TEV “among the great powers.”
Heb “[for many nations] to a distance.”
Instead of referring to the large plow as a whole, the plowshare is simply the metal tip which actually breaks the earth and cuts the furrow.

This implement was used to prune the vines, i.e., to cut off extra leaves and young shoots (M. Klingbeil, NIDOTTE 1:1117-18). It was a short knife with a curved hook at the end sharpened on the inside like a sickle.
Heb “take up the sword.”

verses.zh: 人人都要坐在自己葡萄树下和无花果树下，无人惊吓。这是万军之耶和华亲口说的。
verses.en: Each will sit under his own grapevineor under his own fig tree without any fear.[NOTE:1] The Lord of Heaven’s Armies has decreed it.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and there will be no one making [him] afraid.”
Heb “for the mouth of the Lord…has spoken.”

verses.zh: 万民各奉己神的名而行；我们却永永远远奉耶和华―我们　神的名而行。
verses.en: Though all the nations follow their respective gods,[NOTE:1] we will follow[NOTE:2] the Lord our God forever.
notes: Heb “walk each in the name of his god.” The term “name” here has the idea of “authority.” To “walk in the name” of a god is to recognize the god’s authority as binding over one’s life.
Heb “walk in the name of.”

verses.zh: 耶和华说：到那日，我必聚集瘸腿的，招聚被赶出的和我所惩治的。
verses.en: “In that day,” says the Lord, “I will gather the lameand assemble the outcasts whom I injured.[NOTE:1]
notes: The exiles of the nation are compared to lame and injured sheep.

verses.zh: 我必使瘸腿的为余剩之民，使赶到远方的为强盛之民。耶和华要在锡安山作王治理他们，从今直到永远。
verses.en: I will transform the lame into the nucleus of a new nation[NOTE:1] and those far off[NOTE:2] into a mighty nation.The Lord will reign over them on Mount Zion,from that day forward and forevermore.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “make the lame into a remnant.”

The precise meaning of this difficult form is uncertain. The present translation assumes the form is a Niphal participle of an otherwise unattested denominative verb הָלָא (halaʾ, “to be far off”; see BDB 229 s.v.), but attractive emendations include הַנַּחֲלָה (hannakhalah, “the sick one[s]”) from חָלָה (khalah) and הַנִּלְאָה (hannilʾah, “the weary one[s]”) from לָאָה (laʾah).
Heb “from now until forever.”

verses.zh: 你这羊群的高台、锡安城（原文是女子）的山哪，从前的权柄―就是耶路撒冷民（原文是女子）的国权―必归与你。
verses.en: As for you, watchtower for the flock,[NOTE:1] fortress of Daughter Zion[NOTE:2]—your former dominion will be restored,[NOTE:3] the sovereignty that belongs to Daughter Jerusalem.”
notes: Heb “Migdal Eder.” Some English versions transliterate this phrase, apparently because they view it as a place name (cf. NAB).

The city of David, located within Jerusalem, is addressed as Daughter Zion. As the home of the Davidic king, who was Israel’s shepherd (Ps 78:70-72), the royal citadel could be viewed metaphorically as the watchtower of the flock.
Heb “to you it will come, the former dominion will arrive.”

verses.zh: 现在你为何大声哭号呢？疼痛抓住你彷佛产难的妇人，是因你中间没有君王吗？你的谋士灭亡了吗？
verses.en: Jerusalem, why are you[NOTE:1] now shouting so loudly?[NOTE:2] Has your king disappeared?[NOTE:3] Has your wise leader[NOTE:4] been destroyed?Is this why[NOTE:5] pain grips[NOTE:6] you as if you were a woman in labor?
notes: The Hebrew form is feminine singular, indicating that Jerusalem, personified as a young woman, is now addressed (see v. 10). In v. 8 the tower/fortress was addressed with masculine forms, so there is clearly a shift in addressee here. “Jerusalem” has been supplied in the translation at the beginning of v. 9 to make this shift apparent.
Heb “Now why are you shouting [with] a shout.”
Heb “Is there no king over you?”

Traditionally, “counselor” (cf. KJV, NAB, NASB, NIV84, NRSV); NIV11 “ruler.” This refers to the king mentioned in the previous line; the title points to the king’s roles as chief strategist and policy maker, both of which required extraordinary wisdom.
Heb “that.” The Hebrew particle כִּי (ki) is used here in a resultative sense; for this use see R. J. Williams, Hebrew Syntax, 73, §450.
Heb “grabs hold of, seizes.”

verses.zh: 锡安的民（原文是女子）哪，你要疼痛劬劳，彷佛产难的妇人；因为你必从城里出来，住在田野，到巴比伦去。在那里要蒙解救；在那里耶和华必救赎你脱离仇敌的手。
verses.en: Twist and strain,[NOTE:1] Daughter Zion, as if you were in labor!For you will leave the cityand live in the open field.You will go to Babylon,but there you will be rescued.There the Lord will deliver[NOTE:2] youfrom the power[NOTE:3] of your enemies.
notes: Or perhaps “scream”; NRSV, TEV, NLT “groan.”
Or “redeem” (KJV, NASB, NIV, NRSV, NLT).
Heb “hand.” The Hebrew idiom is a metonymy for power or control.

verses.zh: 现在有许多国的民聚集攻击你，说：愿锡安被玷污！愿我们亲眼见她遭报！
verses.en: Many nations have now assembled against you.They say, “Jerusalem must be desecrated,[NOTE:1] so we can gloat over Zion!”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “let her be desecrated.” The referent (Jerusalem) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “and let our eye look upon Zion.” This is a Hebrew idiom for a typically smug or condescending look by someone in a superior position.

verses.zh: 他们却不知道耶和华的意念，也不明白他的筹划。他聚集他们，好像把禾捆聚到禾场一样。
verses.en: But they do not know what the Lord is planning;they do not understand his strategy.He has gathered them like stalks of grain to be threshed[NOTE:1] at the threshing floor.
notes: The words “to be threshed” are not in the Hebrew text, but have been supplied in the translation to make it clear that the Lord is planning to enable “Daughter Zion” to “thresh” her enemies.

verses.zh: 锡安的民（原文是女子）哪，起来踹谷吧！我必使你的角成为铁，使你的蹄成为铜。你必打碎多国的民，将他们的财献与耶和华，将他们的货献与普天下的主。
verses.en: “Get up and thresh, Daughter Zion!For I will give you iron horns;[NOTE:1] I will give you bronze hooves,and you will crush many nations.”[NOTE:2] You will devote to the Lord the spoils you take from themand dedicate their wealth to the sovereign Ruler[NOTE:3] of the whole earth.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “I will make your horn iron.”
Jerusalem (Daughter Zion at the beginning of the verse; cf. 4:8) is here compared to a powerful ox which crushes the grain on the threshing floor with its hooves.
Or “the Lord” (so many English versions); Heb “the master.”

In vv. 11-13 the prophet jumps from the present crisis (which will result in exile, v. 10) to a time beyond the restoration of the exiles when God will protect his city from invaders. The Lord’s victory over the Assyrian armies in 701 b.c. foreshadowed this.tn Heb “and their wealth to the master of all the earth.” The verb “devote” does double duty in the parallelism and is supplied in the second line for clarification.
